method: Measured from a captured mid-route state, one fresh load per candidate row, about a second each. Five full runs had been spent on this menu beforehand, at roughly six minutes apiece.

row_probe.result: stayed in the submenu, then exited to the party list

conclusion: SWITCH is at field_move_count + 1. With two field moves the five-entry submenu reads moves, moves, STATS, SWITCH, CANCEL — so the order is field moves, then STATS, then SWITCH, then CANCEL, not field moves then SWITCH.

correction_to_earlier_work.what_was_believed: That the submenu ran field moves, then SWITCH, STATS, CANCEL, so SWITCH sat at field_move_count.
correction_to_earlier_work.what_that_caused: The formula was changed from field_move_count + 1 to field_move_count earlier in this session, on the strength of that belief and a five-entry menu that seemed to confirm it. The original formula had been right. The change cost runs and produced a swap that silently did nothing.
correction_to_earlier_work.why_the_belief_survived: Every check available at the time was derived from the same assumption, so nothing could contradict it. The measurement contradicts it in one line.

also_corrected: watched=0x03 was read earlier as meaning the d-pad is ignored. It does not: the party list reports watched=0x03 and its cursor moves normally. That inference was wrong and no conclusion should rest on it.
verification: With the formula restored, swapping slots 1 and 2 from the captured state produces ('0x40', '0x1c', ...) from ('0x1c', '0x40', ...) — the swap that was asked for. Restricting the search to the wrong row turns two harness tests red.
